rounds.report:
Representation level: L1 (proxy). CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline (not equivalent to Blender model rankings).

Observed from the 24 reference samples (0.0-8.76 s): one continuous night shot, no cuts. Over-the-shoulder framing: a man in the foreground at image-left, seen from behind, and a woman standing in the mid-ground right of center, wrapped in a red plaid shawl over a tan coat, white collar and beige trousers, against black darkness with drifting smoke and warm firelight. The man's head turns gradually toward image-right and down from about 4.6 s to 6.5 s, revealing his profile. Both subjects shift upward in frame together after about 5.3 s, which I read as a slow downward camera tilt. The woman sways slightly toward image-right (about 1-3 s) and then back. Focus moves from the woman to the man around 5.3-6.1 s.

Geometry: the woman is a beige leg cylinder, a flattened frustum for the shawl with a rounded shoulder cap, two hanging side panels with fringe strips (the open front shows the trousers), shirt and coat-collar boxes, and a head group (hair ellipsoid with a face ellipsoid). The man is a dark torso box with a shoulder, and an articulated head on a neck pivot: skin skull, dark hair cap offset to the back and top, and a jaw box. There is a dark ground, soft procedural haze planes for smoke and a breath plume, and thin letterbox bars.

Articulation and timing: the man's head yaw (20 to 65 deg toward image-right), pitch (-5 to -26 deg) and small lateral shift, the woman's sway and small head roll, and the camera pitch (0 to -1.6 deg) are all monotone-cubic tracks keyed at the sample timestamps (frame/fps at 24000/1001), so update(time) is absolute and deterministic. The frame count and duration follow the metadata. A deterministic flicker drives the off-screen fire point light.

Inference rather than observation: motion between samples, the fire position, the depth layout (man about 1.1 m from the camera, woman about 4.2 m, vertical FOV 18 deg), and the smoke paths.

Known limitations: there is no depth-of-field blur (the harness owns the renderer), so the focus pull is not reproduced. The plaid pattern is reduced to a flat red. There are no facial features, by the L1 rules.

Render feedback: none received yet (initial round).

Render feedback: round 1 rendered without errors. I compared pairs 00, 14 and 23 and a full-resolution frame. The woman's placement and size already matched. Problems found: the fire light was too orange and oversaturated under ACES, so the shawl and skin turned red; the ground plane created a visible gray horizon and the background haze was too bright; the man's head was about 40 percent too wide and its camera-facing side was unlit. Round 2 revisions: less saturated warm lights and materials, an unlit near-black ground, a dimmer background haze, the man moved back to 1.25 m with a narrower head and the hair cap limited to the top and back, a side light on the camera-facing side of his head, a narrower right shawl panel, and a raised shirt collar.

Its problems were oversaturated orange lighting, a visible ground horizon, an oversized man's head and an unlit side of his head; round 2 fixed these (less saturated lights, an unlit dark ground, the man moved to 1.25 m with a narrower head, a side light). Round 3 revisions: the torso and shoulder moved left under the head, the head x track was shifted left and the final yaw reduced to about 60 deg, the side light on the man's face strengthened and neutralized, skin, hair and shawl albedos desaturated, and the final camera tilt reduced to -1.4 deg.
